issue_context.title: ngDoCheck hook has a bit misleading documentation
issue_context.body:
### Describe the problem that you experienced

Hello,

in my opinion the [documentation regarding the `DoCheck` hook](https://angular.io/api/core/DoCheck) is a bit misleading: 
*A lifecycle hook that invokes a custom change-detection function for a directive, **in addition to the check performed by the default change-detector.***

Text in bold implies that the default check was performed (for the component from which the hook is called), when in fact it doesn't need to be the case. If we have a component with the OnPush change detection strategy, its `ngDoCheck` hook is called from its parent, despite the fact that the default check was not performed on the component.

The following article sums up why ngDoCheck called =/=  change detection performed (it's from 2017, I think that many people fell in the trap of believing that ngDoCheck called = change detection performed):
https://medium.com/angular-in-depth/if-you-think-ngdocheck-means-your-component-is-being-checked-read-this-article-36ce63a3f3e5

@lukasmatta Also related to the formulations here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5693835/202922777-34125e1b-a6dc-4a34-bb2e-22a00c965c28.png)

> If we have a component with the OnPush change detection strategy, its ngDoCheck hook is called from its parent, despite the fact that the default check was not performed on the component.

review_comments:
I'm not sure it 100% clarifies the situation. What is going on here is that the `ngDoCheck` is invoked whenever component _usage_ (in a parent template) is checked. Or to phrase it differently - every time component inputs _might_ have changed.

Alternative phrasing could be:

"A lifecycle hook that invokes a custom change-detection function for a directive,
in addition to the check performed by the default change-detector on the input bindings for this directive usage. Developers might use this hook to implement a custom change detection strategy for some of the inputs."

How does it sound?

@pkozlowski-opensource I would recommend explicitly mentioning two things, the first is that the hook is always run, and the second is that it is possible to overwrite even the implicit decision of the OnPush strategy by the ngDoCheck turn. And also, the described dependencies between hooks and their order should probably be specified (https://angular.io/guide/lifecycle-hooks#lifecycle-event-sequence).

@mlc-mlapis would you mind suggest exact wording?

I'm not sure what you mean by " is possible to overwrite even the implicit decision of the OnPush strategy by the ngDoCheck turn."

> is possible to overwrite even the implicit decision of the OnPush strategy by the ngDoCheck turn.

I mean that the code in the ngDoCheck can change the decision about inputs that are otherwise evaluated as not changed. For example, evaluating some inner properties of an object when its reference is not changed.

@pkozlowski-opensource I agree with the change you suggested, but please note that the misleading information occurs in two more places:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/a6849f27af129588091f635c6ae7a326241344fc/packages/core/src/interface/lifecycle_hooks.ts#L75

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/a6849f27af129588091f635c6ae7a326241344fc/packages/core/src/interface/lifecycle_hooks.ts#L97

I would also consider mentioning the fact that `ngDoCheck` hook is invoked from the parent component (when the change detection runs on the parent component) more explicitly. Although, I am not sure about the precise wording, as I'm not too familiar with the change detection internals (there are maybe some exceptions to this statement).

> change detection runs on the parent component) more explicitly

It's also related to the execution order of the hooks as described in https://angular.io/guide/lifecycle-hooks#lifecycle-event-sequence.

> A lifecycle hook that invokes a custom change-detection function for a directive,
> in addition to the check performed by the default change-detector on the input bindings for this directive usage. Developers might use this hook to implement a custom change detection strategy for some of the inputs.

Sounds good!
